$comment: Build progress for cq itself. If a build of this repo is interrupted, resume from here. Honesty rules: 'tested' means a fixture-driven automated test asserts it; 'smoke_tested' means it was run once against the real CLI by hand; 'untested' means it exists and typechecks but nothing verifies it.
tested: rate_limit_event normalisation: camelCase (as the CLI emits), snake_case (as the brief specified), seconds and milliseconds
classify(): allowed, allowed_warning, rejected, soft utilization threshold, seven_day, overage, unknown status, unknown rate_limit_type
classifyExit(): limit signature on a non-zero exit; no false positive on a clean exit
napFor(): grace, clamping, capped naps for multi-day parks, no busy-loop on a near reset
PARKED -> sleep to resets_at + 60s -> resume via --resume with the reported session_id
allowed_warning finishes the running task and parks before starting the next
seven-day park: notifies once, naps in capped chunks, total sleep lands on the reset
crash isolation: retried 3x with exponential backoff, then failed; daemon exits cleanly
max_turns: requeued exactly once with a hand-off note and the previous session id; never given more turns
a parked run is not charged an attempt
dependency gating, ordering, and transitive blocking of a failed task's dependents
crash reconciliation: a task left running is recovered and resumed, without an attempt charge
a persisted park survives a restart; --force overrides it
inbox: escalation from a summary, answering, unblocking, answer reaching the next prompt
recommendation ingestion bounded by depth (1 generation) and width (5 per run)
stream parser: byte-at-a-time chunking, truncated final line, malformed JSON, unknown event types, arrays and scalars rejected as events
argv construction: --verbose always present with stream-json, model always explicit, capability gating drops unsupported flags
context files: path traversal refused, directories refused, truncation reported in-band, backtick fences cannot be broken out of
queue: validation messages, cycle detection, atomic writes, advisory lock acquire/break/release semantics
plan: extraction from fenced/bare/prose responses, id renumbering, dependency remapping, clamping, repair notes
launchd plist: XML escaping, KeepAlive/ThrottleInterval/RunAtLoad, per-repo labelling
notify: no-op off darwin, never throws, AppleScript escaping, per-key dedupe window
--parallel N: pool fills to N, respects dependency chains, and a park drains in-flight work rather than abandoning it
cq run --parallel is wired from the CLI through to the Scheduler (regression test asserts the wiring itself, which was previously missing)
a timeout is never reclassified as a rate limit, even when the killed process mentions one
an AbortController already aborted before runTask is called still kills the child
a symlink inside the repo pointing outside it is refused by readContextFiles
a park detected while draining concurrent runs is persisted to status.json
an exit-signature park (no reset time) renders no countdown rather than one from 1970
numeric CLI options reject non-numbers and out-of-range values instead of silently becoming NaN
Formula/cq.rb parses, its class name matches the file name, its url version matches package.json, and its sha256 is 64-char hex
smoke_tested: cq init / add / run / status / inbox / inbox answer / logs / doctor against the real CLI in a scratch git repo
one real task on Sonnet: created a file, committed as `cq: t-001 hello.txt`, reported $0.0756 / 3 turns
the CLAUDE.md protocol snippet was detected and the protocol was NOT re-sent (real prompt was 268 characters)
cq plan against the real Opus CLI on examples/city-builder.prompt.md: 20 tasks, $0.9076, one call
cq daemon install / status / uninstall (plist written, read back, removed)
capability probe confirmed cost-free: with no prompt the CLI errors before reaching the API
Homebrew formula from a local tap and a git-archive tarball (Homebrew 7.0.9, macOS arm64): brew install, brew test and brew audit --strict all pass; only commander is vendored
v1.0.0 from the real tap: the GitHub tag archive hashes to the formula's sha256, brew install hareware-labs/tap/cq succeeds and brew test passes (Homebrew 7.0.9, macOS arm64, 2026-10-22)
scripts/release.mjs, both runs, end to end for v1.0.0: bump + formula url + tag, then --formula hashing the pushed archive
untested: cq daemon start/stop under launchd end to end — install, status and uninstall were exercised, but a long-lived agent surviving a real reboot was not
a real seven-day rate limit — only the fixture path is verified; no seven-day window was actually exhausted
resuming a session that the CLI has since expired or garbage-collected
concurrent cq processes in the same repo racing for the lock (the lock is unit-tested; a real race is not)
Node versions other than 22 (CI) and 25 (local). engines declares >=22 and CI proves 22; nothing verifies 20 or 21.
Windows: nothing outside notify and daemon is platform-specific, but only darwin (local) and Linux (CI container) have actually run the suite.
--parallel against the live CLI: the pool is unit-tested and the CLI wiring is asserted, but no real multi-task concurrent run has been made.
The --permission-mode passthrough: wired and visible in --help, but only bypassPermissions has actually been exercised end to end.
scripts/release.mjs has no automated tests; it is exercised only by real releases and hand-run --dry-run
known_limitations: --max-turns is undocumented in the CLI's --help. cq probes for it and falls back to --max-budget-usd, but a silent removal would reduce turn capping to a dollar cap only.

Limit detection from a non-zero exit is a heuristic on stderr text. A task whose own output discusses rate limits can trigger a needless park. It is labelled `detected_by: exit_signature` in status.json and overridable with `cq run --force`.
Only `five_hour` was observable on the account used for development. seven_day_opus, seven_day_sonnet and overage are handled by prefix and by the unknown-type fallback, but were never seen live.
The spend ledger buckets by the five-hour window's reset time. Runs that report no rate_limit_event land in an `unknown` bucket.

Every task runs with --permission-mode bypassPermissions unless `cq run --permission-mode` overrides it. This is disclosed in the README, but it is the largest real-world risk the tool carries: an unattended agent with no prompts, in your repo, under your account.

Recommended tasks come from model output that has read the task's context_files, so text in a read file can influence what gets queued. Bounded to one generation and five tasks, queued behind the human's ordering, and disableable with --no-recommend.
